issues.detail: R2 example expected out=0 on first row despite in=0xFFFFFFFF and prev_in initialized to 0; no 1->0 transition, so out should remain 0. However, R2 condition includes out[i] | (prev_in[i] & ~in[i]); with prev_in=0 and in=0xFFFFFFFF, ~in=0, so out=0. Expected matches. No contradiction.

R3 example: row1 in=1, prev_in=0 -> no falling edge, out=0. row2 in=0, prev_in=1 -> falling edge, out=1. row3 in=1, prev_in=0 -> no falling edge, out holds 1. row4 in=1, prev_in=1 -> no falling edge, out holds 1. Expected [0,1,1,1] matches. No contradiction.

Spec says capture when input changes from 1 to 0; contract uses prev_in initialized to 0. Alternative: prev_in initialized to 1 (or unknown) could cause capture on first row if in=0. Distinguishing sequence: first row reset=0, in=0. Under contract, out=0; under alternative prev_in=1, out=0xFFFFFFFF.
issues.spec_evidence: capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next
issues.alternative: prev_in initialized to all 1s before first sampled posedge

issues.detail: Spec says active high synchronous reset; contract says update_during_reset true and visible same_cycle. Alternative: reset clears out on next cycle (registered reset). Distinguishing sequence: reset=1, in=0xFFFFFFFF then reset=0, in=0. Under contract, out=0 on first row; under alternative, out may be 0xFFFFFFFF on first row then 0.
issues.alternative: reset clears out on the following cycle (registered reset)

issues.detail: R1 spec_quote 'until the register is reset (active high synchronous reset)' is verbatim from S01. R2 and R3 quotes are verbatim. No absent verbatim evidence.
